thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: External auth provider errors detected - token introspection failing (auth0.com).

charlie (oncall): seeing a spike in 401s for console logins. Started triage.
charlie (oncall): logs show repeated failures calling https://auth0.example.com/oauth/introspect -> 502 / connection reset
charlie (oncall): sample error from api-gateway: 
```
ERROR auth.middleware - token introspect failed: net/http: request canceled (client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
request_id=abc123 user_id=unknown
```
charlie (oncall): paging auth owner @sanjay and support @emma. Impact looks like console + some API endpoints that use introspection.

sanjay (auth): ack. I'm looking at Auth0 status now. Their status page shows incidents in eu and us-west endpoints.
charlie (oncall): approx impact: 15-25% of interactive console login attempts failing, service-to-service calls that rely on introspect also returning 401s. Embeddings/async jobs unaffected (use long-lived service tokens).

emma (support): we've already seen ~30 support tickets about "can't log in". Noting customers in EU more affected. Posting to status page: "We are investigating authentication errors for some users due to third-party auth provider disruption."

sanjay (auth): quick root cause hypothesis: our auth flow recently switched from local JWT verification to calling introspection for a short-lived rollout (2026-03-14). If introspect endpoint is down, verification fails.
charlie (oncall): mitigation idea: flip feature flag to skip introspection and fall back to local JWT verification using cached JWKS. Can we do that as a hotfix?

sanjay (auth): yes — we have cached JWKS in the key-cache service. If we bypass introspection and validate locally tokens signed with RS256, we should restore most user logins immediately (unless tokens were opaque).
charlie (oncall): executing hotfix: toggling feature flag auth.use_introspect -> false for web-prod via console.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by charlie: auth-config-hotfix v2026.03.15-00: rollouts: alpha:1, canary:20, prod:100.
charlie (oncall): canary is healthy, rolling to prod now.

charlie (oncall): after the switch, error rate dropped from ~18%->2% for console logins in 10m window.

emma (support): updating status page: "Mitigation in progress: switched to local token verification to restore logins. Auth provider outage still ongoing; some users may need to re-login."

support-bot: created incident ticket INC-20260315-045 with priority P1 and linked support threads.

sanjay (auth): follow-up actions: increase JWKS cache TTL to 10m and add retry/backoff for introspect calls. Also add circuit breaker so introspection failures won't block auth path.
charlie (oncall): agreed. I'll open a follow-up and schedule postmortem.

emma (support): customer impact summary for postmortem: ~120 customers reported login issues, primary effect: web console and some API calls using introspection. No data loss. Mobile apps using SDK with local validation were mostly fine.

dana (oncall-2): taking handoff from charlie for next shift. charlie, status?
charlie (oncall): handing off: hotfix toggled, error rates stabilized, support page updated, ticket created. Next steps: confirm Auth0 full recovery, plan to revert flag when safe, and implement long-term fixes (circuit breaker + improved fallback).

dana (oncall-2): ack. I'll monitor metrics (auth.errors, login.success) and watch for any regressions. Handoff until 07:00 UTC.

incident-bot: New severity update: P1 -> P2 (mitigated) at 2026-03-15T01:26:07Z.

sanjay (auth): Auth0 status now shows partial recovery. Will coordinate with them to get root cause and ETA.

emma (support): support message to customers: "We've implemented a temporary mitigation and most users can log in. We'll revert the mitigation after Auth0 confirms stability. If you still can't log in, please contact support with a screenshot."

charlie (oncall): after Auth0 fully recovers, plan: revert auth.use_introspect flag during a low-traffic window, push a canary, and monitor. Also add a short eval to detect opaque tokens that can't be locally verified and route those to introspection with circuit-breaker.

sanjay (auth): I'll own the follow-up PRs: 1) circuit breaker + retries for introspect, 2) longer JWKS cache TTL with async refresh, 3) an alert when introspect error rate > 1% for 5m.

dana (oncall-2): logging handoff note: incident pinned, will continue to monitor, will update incident timeline and own postmortem.

charlie (oncall): final note — kudos to the quick flip. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED placeholder — mark resolved once flag reverted and Auth0 stable for 24h.
